title: Quantity and diversity of environmental microbial exposure and development of asthma: a birth cohort study.
ehr_evidence: House dust samples were collected at 2 months of age, and health outcomes were assessed using repeated questionnaires and venous blood samples for specific IgE.
summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the association between environmental microbial exposure (quantity and diversity scores from house dust) and the development of asthma, respiratory symptoms, atopic dermatitis, and allergic sensitization in children up to age 6.
key_findings: Total microbial quantity score showed a significant inverted-U-shaped association with asthma incidence (P < 0.001), with the highest risk at medium levels (aOR 2.24, 95% CI 0.87–5.75 for 3rd quintile) and lowest risk at highest levels (aOR 0.34, 95% CI 0.09–1.36 for 5th quintile).
Microbial diversity score was inversely associated with wheezing risk and significantly associated (inverted-U shape) with sensitization to inhalant allergens at age 6.
No significant associations were found between single microbial markers and asthma, respiratory symptoms, atopic dermatitis, or sensitization.
captured_features: house dust microbial markers (endotoxin, muramic acid, ergosterol, β-D-glucan, qPCR for specific bacteria/fungi)
parent-reported respiratory symptoms and asthma diagnoses
population: 410 children born in Eastern and Middle Finland, followed from birth to 6 years of age
exposure_domain: environmental microbial exposure (house dust bacterial and fungal markers)
limitations: lack of adjustment for multiple testing
microbial markers do not capture total microbial exposure without error
potential misclassification of exposure based on single dust sample at 2 months
